summary: Intermittent 5xx spike from runtime exits during low-volume request bursts for Dedicated customer
description: Issue summary: Beginning 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC, Acme Analytics (Dedicated) reported a transient but reproducible increase in 5xx responses for inference calls. Error rate peaked at ~18% for 10 minute windows and manifests primarily as 502/503 returned from our API gateway. Impact: Customer reports failed inference requests for product analytics dashboards during reporting windows (non-blocking but high error rate). Environment: Dedicated pool (dp-acme-01) in us-east-1, serving redwood-v1.3 and llama-2-13b variants. Behavior observed: low-volume burst (dozens of concurrent requests) appears to trigger upstream runtime worker exits; API gateway surfaces 502/503 and occasionally connection resets. Logs show worker processes terminated with SIGKILL and cgroup OOM events around the same timestamps. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send repeated short chat/generation requests (payload ~800 tokens) to the customer's dedicated endpoint at ~10-20 qps for 30s bursts; 2) Observe elevated 5xx; 3) Check runtime node pod logs and dmesg for OOM messages. Initial logs and correlating metrics: - api-gateway: increased 502 counts at 03:12–03:24 UTC. - serving-runtime: worker PID exits, exit code 137, kernel oom_killer messages. - Node memory utilization at node-level hit host memory high watermark; GPU memory remained nominal. - Autoscaler did not spin up additional nodes due to thresholding tied to GPU utilization. Hypothesis: memory pressure on host (not GPU) triggered kernel OOM and killed runtime workers; autoscaler policy only considers GPU saturation so it failed to react to host memory pressure. Alternate hypothesis: a recently deployed model variant increased CPU/memory overhead per worker leading to unexpected host memory growth under bursty traffic. Next steps: 1) Immediate mitigation: restart a subset of runtime nodes in dp-acme-01 and temporarily increase dedicated pool capacity by +2 nodes (manual scale); 2) Apply temporary change to gateway circuit breaker to reduce concurrency to the pool while we stabilize; 3) Add a guard in autoscaler to consider host memory in scale-up decision for the affected pool; 4) Obtain full dmesg/kernel logs from impacted nodes and collect core dumps for one crashed worker for post-analysis. Requested customer actions: avoid scheduled bursts to the dedicated endpoint until we confirm fix and we've applied mitigations.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 03:20 UTC: Support triaged and requested runtime logs. 2026-03-10 04:05 UTC: SRE attached node dmesg showing oom_killer targeting /opt/redwood/worker. 2026-03-10 04:30 UTC: Observed autoscaler decisions - no scale-up triggered because GPU metrics stayed <70%. 2026-03-10 06:10 UTC: Deployed short-term mitigation: +2 nodes to dp-acme-01 and temporarily lowered API gateway concurrent request limit for the pool. 2026-03-10 06:45 UTC: Error rate dropped to <1% after manual scale and circuit breaker change. Hypotheses tested: revert of recent model tweak in staging did not reproduce OOM; reproducer load in staging required host memory exhaustion to trigger kill. Found one recurring pattern: multiple small concurrent sessions cause increased resident set size likely due to KV cache fragmentation and per-session overhead.
resolution: Mitigation applied (2026-03-10 06:30 UTC): manual scale +2 nodes, temp gateway concurrency cap reduced, and affected worker nodes gracefully drained. Result: 5xx rates returned to baseline (<1%). Root cause (provisional): autoscaler policy lacked host-memory-based scale signals; combined with increased per-session host memory usage from a recent model optimization, bursts could exhaust host RAM causing kernel OOM kills of runtime workers. Permanent fixes planned: (1) Update autoscaler to include host memory and oom_count metrics in scale-up decisions (PR submitted), (2) Add per-worker memory limit and graceful eviction instead of allowing kernel OOM, (3) Rework KV cache allocation to be more compact under multi-session workloads for this model family. Follow-up: schedule postmortem and add targeted alerts for host memory pressure on dedicated pools.
resolution_notes: Short-term: increased pool size and gateway limits rolled back to normal on 2026-03-11 after autoscaler patch deployed to staging. Long-term: engineering to ship autoscaler host-memory signal in next sprint; SRE to add runbook steps for host-memory-driven scaling. Customer communication: emailed Acme Analytics w/summary and mitigation 2026-03-10 07:15 UTC.
